scenarios.title: Two Humanoids — Retail Backroom Fulfillment
scenarios.status: Closed — operations accepted; chain rollout held at financial gate
scenarios.summary: Deploy two humanoid robots across the employee-only retail backroom flow. During inbound receiving, a robot-operated forklift removes a full pallet from the delivery truck and clears the work zone; humanoids then carry cartons to lower and raised storage racks, using the visible stair route where required. During fulfillment, a sales associate submits a stock-keeping unit, size, and color request from a tablet; robots pull the requested merchandise and place it on the courtesy drop-off table. Tangled hangers, damaged packaging, ladders, electrical work, and customer-floor operation remain human tasks.
scenarios.decision: The 30-day pilot passed the safety, retrieval, wait-time, inventory-accuracy, damage, intervention, and inbound zone-handoff gates, so Meridian accepted the operating procedure and support handoff. Finance did not authorize chain rollout: modeled annual gross value was $148,258 versus the $346,000 annual value required for five-year payback at the current planning cost. A second-site decision requires a binding vendor quote and either lower recurring cost or independently measured value at or above $346,000 per year.

scenarios.financial_note: There is no positive payback at the pilot inputs. Glassdoor's June 2026 U.S. Retail Sales Associate average salary is $40,242/year, or a $19.35/hour planning equivalent using 2,080 paid hours [RBE-M]. The labor component is 4,965 hours × $19.3471 = $96,058. Adding $52,200 of fictional measured margin recovery produces $148,258 annual gross value, below the $218,000 recurring cost. Five-year payback requires $346,000 annual gross value: $218,000 recurring cost plus $128,000 annual recovery of the $640,000 installation. The Glassdoor benchmark is crowd-sourced and excludes Meridian benefits, location, and payroll; robot, integration, license, and support prices remain planning allowances pending binding quotes.

demo.title: MuJoCo Retail Backroom Humanoid Simulation
demo.caption: A 40-second, seven-stage MuJoCo retail-backroom story. A robot-operated forklift backs a full pallet out of the delivery truck and parks it in receiving. After the forklift clears the zone, two humanoids carry cartons to lower and raised storage racks; the upper-route robot visibly climbs each of four physical treads. The scene then cuts to order fulfillment: both robots pull requested merchandise and place it on the courtesy drop-off table for a sales associate. On-video stage labels make the workflow explicit. Scripted motion is not locomotion, grasp, forklift-control, collision-avoidance, or safety-performance validation. [DC-L; Low confidence]
sequence: Unload truck: robot-operated forklift removes full pallet
Clear receiving zone and verify stable pallet
Stock lower and raised racks; use visible stairs where required
Receive tablet order and confirm item location
Pull requested merchandise from both stock levels
Place merchandise on courtesy drop-off table
Update inventory and accept next mission

scenarios.title: Three Quadrupeds — Night Security
scenarios.summary: Deploy three quadruped robots for human-supervised night patrol across stairs, curbs, gravel, and narrow walkways. Two robots run scheduled perimeter routes while the third rotates through charging and reserve coverage. Robots observe and report; authorized human security personnel retain all response decisions.
scenarios.decision: The pilot met all safety, privacy, patrol, alert, geofence, availability, and docking criteria. Sentinel Ridge authorized two recurring quadruped patrol posts and retained the existing fixed-post responder. Expansion beyond the approved routes requires a new route, privacy, network, and benefit review.
scenarios.financial_note: The May 2025 U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics national mean wage for security guards is $20.42 per hour [PB-H]; it is only a wage benchmark. The fictional $45 contractor invoice is 2.20 times that wage because it is assumed to include burden, supervision, insurance, overhead, and margin [SA-L]. With two 10-hour rover posts and a $15K vehicle, payback is 3.22 years, discounted payback is 3.88 years, and five-year Net Present Value at 8% is $174,099 [DC-L]. The five-year break-even invoice rate is $33.98/hour. At one removed post, payback is 11.73 years and the decision fails. Actual invoices, contract-change rights, routes, costs, and realized savings are [UPV].

scenarios.title: Open-Source Quadruped to Supported RaaS
scenarios.status: Closed - limited availability approved; scale gate conditional
scenarios.tco: $184.8K customer three-year RaaS TCO for two robots
scenarios.summary: Convert the Open Dynamic Robot Initiative Solo12 research reference into a supported supervised-laboratory Robotics-as-a-Service offer. The provider adds controlled sourcing, assembly and calibration, battery and emergency-stop integration, signed images, Software Bill of Materials and license notices, telemetry, a replacement pool, onboarding, service levels, and release governance without claiming upstream endorsement or industrial certification.
scenarios.decision: The six-site, 12-robot pilot passed the fictional reproducibility, safety-state, availability, experiment-completion, service, and open-source release gates. Limited availability is approved for the controlled laboratory envelope. General Availability remains held until at least 48 robots are contracted at or above the $2,384.57 monthly price floor, two electronics second sources are qualified, and customer time studies, audited unit/service costs, and independent compliance review replace planning assumptions.

metrics.note: Internal release audit; independent review still pending

scenarios.financial_note: Glassdoor's May 2026 U.S. Robotics Software Engineer benchmark is $154,709/year or $74/hour [PB-M]. BLS reports private-industry wages at 69.9% of compensation in March 2026 [PB-H], producing a $221,329 loaded planning cost before the fictional staffing mix [DC-M]. Unitree's official $15,900 Go2 EDU price is a current research-quadruped comparator [PB-M], not a Solo12 quote. The resulting $2.397M program, $24K unit cost, $12.672K 36-month service cost, $2,400 monthly price, 48-unit recovery gate, $184.8K two-robot TCO, and 20.1% customer ROI are [DC-L] because staffing, hours, allowances, utilization, and demand are [SA-L]. Executed contracts, customer time studies, audited costs, and realized cash savings remain mandatory.

scenarios.title: Robotics Support & Field Operations
scenarios.status: Closed — service owner accepted operating model
scenarios.summary: Stand up one traceable support chain for 250 humanoid and quadruped robots across 60 sites. The operating model connects Salesforce customer cases, ServiceNow or Zendesk workflows, field work, Jira engineering defects, robot telemetry, parts, knowledge, release readiness, and customer communications.
scenarios.decision: The executive sponsor and service owner accepted the 180-day operating model. All 250 robots and 60 sites have owned installed-product records; severity, on-call, field, parts, remote-access, continuity, and product-readiness controls are live. High-confidence predictive case automation remains a phase-two improvement and is not required for closeout.

scenarios.title: Two Humanoids — Airport Restroom Cleaning Pilot
scenarios.status: Phase 1 Amber; Phase 2 RaaS Conditional Green
scenarios.summary: Deploy two humanoid robots into four unchanged Terminal 4 public restrooms for controlled routine cleaning and replenishment. The rooms remain closed and verified empty during robot work. Airport custodians retain inspection, prohibited-contamination response, corrective cleaning, supply custody, and reopening authority. The program is managed through three coordinated viewpoints: seller/integrator, humanoid manufacturer, and airport buyer/operator.
scenarios.decision: Phase 1 closed Amber: the four-room pilot passed its technical and operating gates but $68,985 of annual capacity value did not support its $3.1345 million five-year capital-purchase path. Phase 2 is a separate Conditional Green recommendation: two robots serve 12 restrooms for 28 productive fleet-hours per day under Robotics-as-a-Service. At $6,000 per robot per month, planning five-year Total Cost of Ownership is $1.270 million, net benefit is $339,650, and Return on Investment is 26.7%. Proceed only after workload validation and binding quotes at or below the $6,595 monthly customer ceiling.

scenarios.financial_note: The May 2025 U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics national mean wage for janitors and cleaners is $18.64/hour [PB-H]. The airport's $31.50 loaded task rate is a fictional customer assumption [SA-L], not a BLS value. Phase 1 creates only $68,985 of annual capacity against a $3.1345M capital-path five-year TCO and fails. The separate Phase 2 RaaS case assumes 28 productive fleet-hours/day, $6K per robot-month, $150K integration, and $80K annual retained human support. It produces $339,650 five-year net benefit, 26.7% ROI, about $241,006 NPV at 8%, and 1.53-year simple payback [DC-L]. Break-even is 22.1 productive hours/day; at 22 hours the case is slightly negative, and at the public mean wage even 28 hours/day does not cover the modeled annual run cost. Capacity is not cash savings; workload, prices, performance, and realization remain [UPV].
